theoretical_floor.warning: This optimistic whole-device cold-HBM normalization is not a dispatch-latency lower bound. Tiny fixed tiles cannot saturate all 256 CUs or peak HBM bandwidth.

ablations.name: exact-tile proof-directed global loads
ablations.detail: The checked exact-view proof removes 32 per-fragment guarded loads while partial tiles retain zero-fill guards. FP4 GEMM improved from 19401 ns to 7400 ns (2.6218x); FP8 GEMM improved from 17320 ns to 6800 ns (2.5471x). Attention shapes do not satisfy this GEMM-only proof and changed by less than four percent, providing a control for run-to-run variance.

ablations.name: four-waves-per-workgroup and four-workgroup grid
ablations.detail: WG256/grid4 is the smallest currently proven multi-wave launch for these collective fragments.

ablations.name: two-waves-per-workgroup and eight-workgroup grid
ablations.detail: The production verifier reported UnprovenBarrierConvergence for the MFMA collective; no runtime number is reported.

ablations.name: eight-waves-per-workgroup and two-workgroup grid
ablations.detail: Typed V1 admits workgroup sizes only through 256; no runtime number is reported.

ablations.name: software-pipelined LDS double buffering
ablations.detail: K=128 is exactly one native MFMA reduction tile. There is no next K tile to overlap, so a second LDS stage would duplicate the only tile.

ablations.name: pretransposed rhs through an 8 KiB LDS transpose tile
ablations.detail: The variant was numerically exact and exercised the gfx950 transpose path, but its FP8 GEMM median was 21001 ns versus 6800 ns for direct exact-tile global loads, a 3.0884x regression. Weight-prepack time was excluded from both measurements.
